title: Canonical Schema Views for Activation Steering Under Tool-Schema Churn: A Negative Result

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The stated purpose is to save future researchers from pursuing schema canonicalization as a route to churn-invariant activation steering for tool-calling. This requires identifying prior work that empirically establishes the same relationship: that schema canonicalization fails to provide robustness benefits under schema perturbations. Paper [7] discusses schema misalignment in tool-calling but does not empirically establish the failure of canonicalization as a robustness strategy. Paper [6] introduces canonicalization for equivariance but does not address robustness under schema perturbations. Paper [24] addresses schema evolution in text-to-SQL models but does not empirically evaluate canonicalization's robustness. No prior paper establishes the same empirical relationship.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves transforming tool schemas to generic placeholder identifiers (e.g., `tool_0(arg_0_0, arg_0_1)`) before ASA calibration and inference, remapping outputs back to real identifiers. Paper [8] introduces delexicalized sentence generation for slot filling, which replaces slot values with slot labels, a substantively equivalent mechanism of placeholder substitution. Paper [14] discusses iterative delexicalization for spoken language understanding, which similarly replaces variable content with abstract placeholders. Both papers use the same underlying primitive of delexicalization/remapping.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring AST accuracy degradation and robustness under schema perturbations using BFCL v3. Paper [24] evaluates text-to-SQL robustness under schema evolution, which involves schema perturbations, making the evaluation design substantively equivalent. Paper [28] benchmarks robustness to perturbations in a different domain (image classifiers), but the evaluation design (perturbation-based robustness testing) is equivalent. Both papers match the evaluation design.

### Domain
The domain is LLM tool-calling and activation steering robustness. Paper [7] explicitly addresses schema misalignment in tool-calling for small language models, which falls within the same application area. Paper [9] discusses activation steering robustness in language models, which also matches the domain. Both papers cover the domain.
